data.author: @gogodev2
data.content: Over the past few months, I've gone deep down the insane rabbit hole of DMCA, cryptographic protocols for copyright protection, TEEs, secure worlds, untrusted computing, and so on... and I've come to the conclusion that the future won't be kind to us. I think what will define the coming years is this question: "Do most people actually care about having a computer that can do things on its own, and about actually owning those things? Or would they be perfectly happy with an extremely underpowered black box that has almost nothing beyond a TPM chip and just enough hardware to connect to servers that handle everything for them?" The future could be bleak.

data.content: 0:47 I've spent the last few weeks reverse-engineering my TV, which runs a closed system. I managed to make quite a bit of progress until I hit a wall with the TEE, and other important components, like the kernel itself, are encrypted. Now I'm trying to find vulnerabilities, implementation flaws, and observe how the TEE responds to different inputs to see if I can get past this barrier. I'll probably have to work directly on the circuit board, but the whole experience has been really valuable.
